summary: NexaHealth: stepwise tuning, hotfix and controlled backout plan for batching/prefix-cache/quant profile causing sporadic tail-latency spikes
description: Issue summary: Customer NexaHealth reports intermittent 95th/99th percentile tail-latency spikes (~800-1200ms) on streaming generate endpoints after enabling a new optimizer bundle (quant profile 'q3-fast', aggressive prefix prefetch, tenant max_batch_size=128). Impact: production user-facing latency spikes affecting interactive workflows and causing occasional client perceived timeouts. Environment: Dedicated pool in prod-us-east for tenant NexaHealth. Recent change: on 2026-03-09 at ~03:10 UTC tenant-specific optimizer profile applied via console (profile=q3-fast, prefetch=aggressive, batching.max_size=128).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use tenant NexaHealth prod endpoint with streaming generate API and 1-2 parallel clients sending variable-length prompts similar to customer's workload.
2) Observe P50/P95/P99 token latencies over 30-60 minutes while q3-fast + prefix prefetch=aggressive + max_batch_size=128 are active.
3) Compare to baseline profile (q2-safe, prefetch=standard, max_batch_size=32) and note increase in 95/99 percentiles.
4) Reproduce more easily by sending bursty short prompts that trigger small-batch warmups and prefix cache evictions.
investigation_notes: 03/10 09:45 - Collected p99 latency histograms from tenant routing logs and per-instance traces; spikes correlate with cache eviction events and larger batch formation windows.
03/10 11:20 - Heap and GPU metrics show no OOM but increased kernel-launch variability under q3-fast quantization on one node type (A10x).
03/11 02:30 - Found prefix-cache aggressive prefetch config causing frequent background eviction/refresh cycles for high-turnover tenants; eviction coincides with increased backend tail latency.

Hypothesis: q3-fast quant kernels are more sensitive to sequence length variance and interleaved EV/KB cache churn, producing higher per-token jitter for tail requests when combined with large max_batch_size and aggressive prefetch.
comments: Sofia Ramirez (2026-03-10 10:02): Customer opened chat saying "We started seeing slow responses intermittently after the optimizer tweak; interactive UI users notice lag." Asked for sample request IDs and recent config.
Ethan Cole (2026-03-10 10:30): Collected tenant traces and configured short-term debug logging on two serving nodes. Assigned to SRE to validate cache eviction cadence.
NexaHealth CS (2026-03-10 11:05): Provided sample request IDs and confirmed they had rolled the profile to production via console change on 2026-03-09.

SRE Lead - Priya Shah (2026-03-11 02:50): Recommends staged rollback of quant profile to q2-conservative + reduce max_batch_size and pause aggressive prefix prefetch as a hotfix. Will coordinate with customer for a maintenance window.
recommended_action: Hotfix plan (stepwise, non-disruptive): 1) Apply quant profile backout for tenant: set optimizer.quant_profile=q2-conservative for NexaHealth first. 2) Reduce tenant batching.max_size to 32 and enable batching.timeout_ms=20. 3) Set prefix_cache.prefetch=standard (disable aggressive prefetch). 4) Monitor P95/P99 for 30 minutes; if improved, promote config to all instances for tenant. Rollback commands examples: redwoodctl tenant update-config --tenant nexahealth --set optimizer.quant_profile=q2-conservative; redwoodctl tenant update-config --tenant nexhealth --set batching.max_size=32
workaround: If immediate mitigation needed and customer agrees to short maintenance window, toggle tenant routing fallback to the 'q2-safe' model variant (route policy -> model_fallback = q2-safe) while applying config changes. This avoids cluster-wide changes.
postmortem_tasks: 1) Add automated pre-deployment canary checks for quant-profile + prefetch combinations that historically increase kernel variance.
2) Instrument prefix-cache eviction metrics into tenant dashboard and add alert if eviction rate > threshold for 5m.
3) Update optimizer docs to call out interactions between large batch sizes and aggressive prefetch on mixed-length workloads.
4) Run controlled load-test for q3-fast on representative hardware to quantify tail behaviour across sequence distributions.
notes: Next steps: schedule 20-minute maintenance window with NexaHealth for staged hotfix (requested window 2026-03-13 02:00-02:30 UTC). SRE to run hotfix and report metrics back via this ticket. If hotfix fails to remediate, escalate to Applied ML for kernel profiling and possible model quant kernel patch.
